load.brokenTitle: The configuration could not be read: {{error}}
load.brokenBackup: A copy of the previous file is at {{path}}.
load.brokenNoBackup: No backup copy could be written.
load.brokenDefaults: The defaults are shown. The original file is untouched — only saving replaces it.
load.missingHint: Saving creates it with these values.
load.warningsTitle: The configuration was read, with notes:

status.reloadHint: Reload first restores the previous light state, then rebuilds everything from the file.
status.noDevices: No devices active. Create one under “Devices”, then reload.
status.logNote: The last 500 lines from the engine.

audio.inputNote: Which device is listened to. For music the output device is recorded, not a microphone.
audio.deviceNote: “System default” follows the Windows setting and changes along with it.
audio.byName: Match by name instead of id
audio.byNameText: Pick the device by part of its name
audio.byNameNote: The id survives renaming a device, the name survives a driver change. The name is matched as a substring.
audio.deviceReadFailed: The audio devices could not be read: {{error}}
audio.analysisNote: How the signal is broken into a spectrum. Larger windows resolve low notes better but react more slowly.
audio.fftSizeNote: Rounded up to the next power of two between 64 and 16384. 1024 at 48 kHz is about 21 ms per window.
audio.hopSizeNote: Distance between two analysis windows in samples. Equal to the FFT size means no overlap. Smaller is smoother and costs more.
audio.downmixNote: How the channels collapse into the one signal the brightness comes from. The spatial distribution keeps working on the individual channels regardless.
audio.bufferNote: WASAPI buffer in 100 ns units. 200000 is 20 ms. Larger is less prone to dropouts but slower to react.
audio.silenceNote: What happens when nothing is playing any more.
audio.silenceAfterNote: This long without audio counts as silence.
audio.silenceBrightnessNote: 0 turns the lights off, 1 leaves them at full brightness.

windows.hann: Hann — the default, a good compromise

apps.title: Capture individual applications
apps.note: Instead of the whole output device, only certain programs. Windows only; elsewhere the device is captured as before.
apps.enabledText: Only listen to the applications named below

modes.exclude: Capture everything except the named applications

apps.treeText: Also capture a child process of a match
apps.treeNote: Browsers play through a child process with a different name. On Windows child processes are always captured, so this option has no effect there.
apps.rescanNote: How often newly started programs are looked for. Minimum 250 ms.
apps.sampleRateNote: Per-process capture has no mix format of its own, so it records in the output device's unless a rate is stated here.
apps.channelsNote: Same again: without a number this records in as many channels as the output device runs in. A 7.1 output pinned to 2 here is what makes the status line read stereo.
apps.groupsNote: Each group names programs and its own gain. Matching ignores case and is done against the display name and the .exe.
apps.noGroups: No group yet. Without a group naming at least one program, the device is captured as before.
apps.programsNote: One entry per line, e.g. “chrome.exe”, “spotify” or part of the display name.
apps.gainNote: Factor applied to this group's samples before they are mixed with the others.
apps.runningNote: What currently has an audio session open. A click copies the name into the first group.
apps.appsReadFailed: The applications could not be read: {{error}}

colors.bandsNote: The spectrum is summarised into these bands. A band without its own colour takes it from the colour stops below, measured at its centre frequency.
colors.noBands: Without bands the built-in three apply: bass, mid, treble.
colors.mapNote: Which colour a frequency gets. Everything between the stops is interpolated.
colors.stopNote: Stops with an equal or non-positive frequency are discarded at startup.
colors.saturationNote: How far the mixed colour is pushed back to full saturation. Without it the bands land near grey, because each is normalised against its own level.
colors.valueSpanNote: How much brightness the level adds on top.
colors.fallbackNote: Used when nothing is playing, or when neither a stop nor a band colour can answer.

interpolations.srgb: sRGB — straight between the colour values

white.off: Off — the white channel stays dark

dynamics.normNote: How the raw spectrum becomes a value between 0 and 1.
dynamics.referenceNote: “Per band” lets quiet treble shine too; “shared” keeps the ratio between the bands as it sounds.

normalize.shared: Shared — one level for every band
normalize.per_band: Per band — each band against its own level

dynamics.logOffsetNote: Offset in the loudness compression ln(x + offset). Larger values lift quiet passages.
dynamics.peakFloorNote: Lower bound of the level tracker, and the noise threshold.
dynamics.peakDecayNote: How quickly the remembered peak falls back. Near 1 means very slow.
dynamics.envNote: How quickly a band brightens and falls back. Clamped to 0.01–1.0 at startup.
dynamics.beatNote: Detection of sudden energy gains, and what happens then.
dynamics.beatThresholdNote: Lower detects more beats, and more false ones. Clamped below 1.
dynamics.beatCooldownNote: No further beat is detected for this long. 0 disables the cooldown.
dynamics.strobeColorNote: Without its own colour the strobe keeps the colour of the music.

output.rateNote: How often the lights hear anything at all. Too fast and a Shelly cannot keep up over Wi-Fi.
output.intervalNote: Lower bound between two commands, shared by every device.
output.beatWeightNote: How much a detected beat shortens the transition.
output.curveNote: 1 is linear, larger shifts the transition toward the long times.
output.deadbandNote: How small a change may be before it is not sent at all. Saves radio traffic and keeps the lights calm.
output.limitsNote: These apply globally and bound what an individual device can set. The per-device values are under “Devices”.
output.floorNote: No device goes below this while something is playing.

spatial.viewNote: Dragging with the left mouse button turns the view, the wheel zooms. A click selects a light; the handle moves it. On a strip that runs around a corner, every corner ball can be dragged on its own; the marker in the middle moves the whole strip. In turn mode a click on a run turns that run, hinged at the corner it starts from.
spatial.disabledHint: The spatial distribution is switched off — positions can be set here but only take effect once it is enabled below.
spatial.geometryNote: The same values as under “Devices”, here next to the view.
spatial.viewFailed: The room view could not be displayed.
spatial.viewFailedNote: Usually 3D acceleration is missing — in a remote session, for instance. Positions can still be typed in as numbers.
spatial.distributionNote: Spreads the music across the room: a light on the left follows the left channel. Only takes effect once a device also has a position.
spatial.enabledText: Take the device positions into account
spatial.focusNote: How sharply a light hears only its nearest speaker. Higher separates more. Clamped to 0.1–16.
spatial.omniFloorNote: How much of the overall mix each light keeps regardless of its position. 0 isolates completely.
spatial.heightSharpnessNote: How clearly a light's height in the room maps to bass low and treble high. Clamped to 0.05–4.
spatial.distanceFalloffNote: How much a more distant light dims. 0 disables it.
spatial.stripSamplesNote: How finely a strip is sampled along its length. Clamped to 1–256.
spatial.roomNote: The bounds of the room in metres. The listening position is the origin, +X right, +Y up, +Z to the front.
spatial.layoutNote: Normally read from the audio device's channel mask. Only needed by hand when the driver reports nonsense — then one entry per capture channel, in channel order.

forms.lamp: Lamp — a point in the room
forms.strip: Strip — a line in the room

geometry.pathNote: This strip runs around a corner, so it is described by the corners it passes through instead of a centre and a direction.
geometry.legNote: Each run between two corners has its own length and direction. Changing one hinges the strip at the corner it starts from: everything after it comes along unchanged.
geometry.pathEditNote: A new corner continues from the last leg, a quarter turn to the right. Straightening keeps the line from the first corner to the last.
geometry.bendNote: Turns this strip into a corner list: its two ends, plus one leg of the same length around the corner. Length and orientation are then stated per corner.
geometry.lengthNote: End to end. The position marks the middle.
geometry.orientationNote: Turn: 0° points at the front wall, 90° to the right. Tilt: 0° horizontal, 90° straight up.
geometry.positionedText: This device sits at a fixed place in the room
geometry.positionedNote: Without a position the device follows the overall mix, whatever is set under “Room”.
geometry.spatialityNote: How far this device follows its position rather than the overall mix. At 0 the position has no effect.
geometry.advancedHint: To aim it in the 3D view: the Room tab, where a strip can also be led around a corner. Tilt against the height mapping, an own focus and an own distance falloff are set through the JSON view (elevation_tilt, focus, distance_falloff).

devices.emptyNote: Without a device the analysis runs but drives nothing.
devices.addNote: The list comes from the engine's registry — a new driver in src-tauri/src/devices/ shows up here by itself.
devices.testOkNote: The light flashed white for a moment and is back as it was.
devices.noSchema: There is no form for the type “{{type}}” here. The entry is kept in full and can be edited as JSON.
devices.jsonObject: It has to be a JSON object.

fields.gammaNote: Below 1 lifts quiet passages, above 1 pushes them down. Bounded by the global limits under “Output”.
fields.name: Name
fields.modelNote: “Detect automatically” asks the device itself at startup.
fields.channelNote: Number of the RGBW output on the device.
fields.bridgeNote: Address of the Hue bridge in the network. The IP shown in the Hue app under Settings › Bridge.
fields.applicationKeyNote: Handed out by the bridge when pairing. It stays valid, so this only has to be done once per bridge.
fields.hueRateNote: The bridge forwards about ten commands a second per light; anything faster is dropped. Frames in between are skipped, the newest one is sent.
fields.hueTransitionsText: Let the light fade into the new colour
fields.hueTransitionsNote: Off makes every change a jump: harsher, but it follows the beat more closely.
fields.verifyTlsNote: A bridge signs its own certificate, which no certificate store knows. Leave this off unless the bridge has one of its own.
fields.hueBridgeActionsNote: Press the round button on the bridge, then pair within half a minute.
fields.huePairOk: Paired. The application key is filled in.
fields.hueFoundNote: A click adds a light to this device or takes it off again.
fields.hueSelectedNote: With a gradient each light takes one colour, in the order they stand here.
fields.dreamviewText: Switch into Razer/DreamView mode for the session
fields.dreamviewNote: Lifts the rate limit Govee otherwise puts on colour changes. Taken back on exit.
fields.colorTempNote: 0 keeps the light in RGB mode.
fields.localBindNote: Fixed by the first Govee device and then used by all of them. A change only takes effect after restarting the app.
fields.segmentsDreamNote: At most 15. Segment addressing over LAN is not part of the documented API — if the strip does not follow, enter 1 here.
fields.segmentsWledNote: How many colours the strip shows, not how many LEDs it has. 1 makes the whole strip one colour.
fields.ledsNote: Without a value it is read from the controller over HTTP at startup.
fields.protocolNote: Only DNRGB reaches pixels beyond 490. DRGBW for an RGBW strip.
fields.realtimeTimeoutNote: This long after the last packet WLED resumes its own effect. If the strip falls back, raise this.
fields.authText: The device requires a user name and a password
fields.authNote: Stored in plain text in the configuration file, because the device's digest authentication needs the original password.

advanced.themeNote: “Follow the system” tracks the Windows setting, even while the app is open.
advanced.languageNote: Applies to the window and the tray menu. The engine's log stays English.
advanced.pathNote: Recorded in app.json next to this setting. A --config argument or SHELLYRGBAUDIO_CONFIG still takes precedence.
advanced.jsonNote: For anything without a field above — per-device colour or band overrides, for instance. Changes here reach the disk on save like any other.
advanced.resetNote: Replaces the shown configuration with the built-in defaults. The file on disk stays until you save.
advanced.resetDoneNote: The file is still unchanged. Use “Discard” to go back, or save to keep them.
